title: A Study of HS-20110 in Participants With Advanced Solid Tumors
official: A Phase I Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Efficacy of HS-20110 in Participants With Advanced Solid Tumors
summary: This is an open-label, multicenter study to evaluate the safety and tolerability of HS-20110 in participants with advanced solid malignant tumors

interventions.name: HS-20110 in combination with bevacizumab, 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), and leucovorin.
HS-20110 in combination with bevacizumab, 5-FU, and leucovorin.

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Males or females, aged ≥ 18 years.
2. Participants with pathologically (histologically or cytologically) confirmed advanced solid tumors.
3. Participants have at least 1 target lesion other than CNS lesions according to RECIST 1.1 and not intended to be biopsied.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Participants have received or are receiving the following treatment:

   1. Previous or concurrent treatment with any CDH17-targeting therapy, including small molecules, monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), or CAR-T cell therapy.
   2. Cytotoxic chemotherapy, traditional Chinese medicine with anti-tumor indications, or other anti-tumor drugs within 14 days before the first dose; or other investigational medicinal products (IMPs) or macromolecular anti-tumor drugs (e.g., monoclonal antibodies, ADCs, or bispecific antibodies) within 28 days before the first dose. Continued treatment with these drugs during the study is also not permitted.
   3. Local radiotherapy within 2 weeks before the first dose, or radiotherapy involving \>30% of the bone marrow or extensive radiotherapy within 4 weeks before the first dose.
   4. Major surgery within 4 weeks before the first dose.
   5. Use of moderate-to-strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers, or strong inhibitors of CYP2D6, P-glycoprotein (P-gp), breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B1 (OATP1B1), or OATP1B3 within 7 days before the first dose, or requiring these medications during the study.
   6. Current use of medications known to prolong the QT interval or cause torsade de pointes, or anticipated use of such medications during the study.
   7. Receipt of live or live-attenuated vaccines within 28 weeks before the first dose.
2. Participants who have any persistent treatment-related toxicity of Grade ≥2 according to the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI CTCAE) v5.0, except for alopecia and residual neurotoxicity.
3. Inadequate bone marrow, hepatic, or renal function.
4. Participants with a history of severe allergic reactions, severe infusion-related reactions, or known allergy to recombinant human or murine proteins.
5. Participants who has known allergy or hypersensitivity to any component of HS-20110.
